name: Micro Finance Scheme (MFS)
overview: Micro-credit for eligible small business units costing up to ₹1.40 lakh. The beneficiary loan is up to 90% of project cost, capped at ₹1.25 lakh.
keyBenefits: Beneficiary interest rate: 6.5% p.a.
Quarterly repayment within 3 years, including a 3-month moratorium
Applications go through an authorized SCA or channel agency
mandatoryDocuments: SC certificate issued by a competent authority
Income proof for the current family-income limit
KYC documents and bank account details
Business activity estimate or quotation
eligibilityBullets: Applicant belongs to the Scheduled Caste community
Annual family income is at or below ₹5 lakh
Project cost is at or below ₹1.40 lakh
repaymentTerms: Quarterly instalments; up to 3 years including moratorium

name: Aajeevika Micro-Finance Yojana (AMY)
overview: Need-based micro-finance for eligible Scheduled Caste applicants through selected NBFC-MFIs for small and micro business activities.
keyBenefits: Projects up to ₹1.40 lakh; loan up to ₹1.25 lakh
Beneficiary interest rate: 15% p.a.
Quarterly repayment within 3 years, including a 3-month moratorium
mandatoryDocuments: SC certificate issued by a competent authority
Income proof for the current family-income limit
KYC documents and bank account details
Business activity estimate or quotation
eligibilityBullets: Applicant belongs to the Scheduled Caste community
Annual family income is at or below ₹5 lakh
Project cost is at or below ₹1.40 lakh
Availability depends on a selected NBFC-MFI
repaymentTerms: Quarterly instalments; up to 3 years including moratorium

name: Udyam Nidhi Yojana (UNY)
interestRateNote: 13% through cooperative banks/societies; 15% through small finance banks.
overview: Loans for small and micro activities with project costs up to ₹5 lakh, through cooperative societies, cooperative banks, and small finance banks.
keyBenefits: Loan up to 90% of project cost, capped at ₹4.50 lakh
Beneficiary rate depends on lender: 13% or 15% p.a.
Quarterly or half-yearly repayment within 5 years, including a 3-month moratorium
mandatoryDocuments: SC certificate issued by a competent authority
Income proof for the current family-income limit
KYC documents and bank account details
Business activity estimate or quotation
eligibilityBullets: Applicant belongs to the Scheduled Caste community
Annual family income is at or below ₹5 lakh
Project cost is at or below ₹5 lakh
Availability depends on an eligible cooperative lender or small finance bank
repaymentTerms: Quarterly or half-yearly instalments; up to 5 years including moratorium

name: Term Loan Scheme
overview: Term loans for viable income-generating units costing more than ₹1.40 lakh and up to ₹50 lakh.
keyBenefits: Loan up to 90% of project cost, capped at ₹45 lakh
Beneficiary interest rate: 8% p.a.
Quarterly repayment within 7 years, including a 6-month moratorium (12 months for plantation and construction)
mandatoryDocuments: SC certificate issued by a competent authority
Income proof for the current family-income limit
KYC documents and bank account details
Project report and supplier quotations, as required by the channel agency
eligibilityBullets: Applicant belongs to the Scheduled Caste community
Annual family income is at or below ₹5 lakh
Project cost is above ₹1.40 lakh and at or below ₹50 lakh
Project must be viable and approved by the channel agency
repaymentTerms: Quarterly instalments; up to 7 years including moratorium

name: Educational Loan Scheme (ELS)
overview: Education loans for eligible students pursuing recognized, full-time professional or technical courses in India or abroad.
keyBenefits: Up to ₹40 lakh or 90% of course fees, whichever is lower
Beneficiary interest rate: 6.5% p.a.
Up to 12 years to repay where repayment has not started; moratorium is course duration plus one year
mandatoryDocuments: SC certificate issued by a competent authority
Income proof for the current family-income limit
KYC documents and bank account details
Recognized institution admission letter and course fee schedule
eligibilityBullets: Applicant belongs to the Scheduled Caste community
Annual family income is at or below ₹5 lakh
Admission is to an eligible, recognized full-time professional or technical course
Loan is capped at 90% of course fees and ₹40 lakh
repaymentTerms: Up to 12 years when repayment has not started; otherwise up to 10 years
moratoriumTerms: Course period plus 1 year, where repayment has not started

name: Sanitation Workers Rehabilitation Scheme (SWRS)
overview: Term loans for eligible sanitation workers currently engaged in sewerage or drainage work to acquire mechanized sanitation equipment and related income-generating assets.
keyBenefits: Up to 90% of a unit cost of ₹15 lakh
Beneficiary interest rate: 5% p.a.
Repayment up to 10 years after implementation and moratorium periods
mandatoryDocuments: Proof of eligible sanitation-worker status
KYC documents and bank account details
Income and other documents requested by the channel agency
Equipment quotation and project details
eligibilityBullets: Applicant belongs to the scheme’s eligible sanitation-worker target group
Proposed activity concerns mechanized sanitation or a related viable project
The channel agency verifies worker status and project eligibility
repaymentTerms: Up to 10 years, subject to project viability

name: Credit Enhancement Guarantee Scheme for Scheduled Castes
hindiName: अनुसूचित जातियों के लिए ऋण वृद्धि गारंटी योजना

financialHighlights.label: Guarantee cover
financialHighlights.note: This is the guarantee cover range, not a direct loan amount.

financialHighlights.label: Guarantee period
financialHighlights.note: Or the loan repayment period, whichever is earlier.

financialHighlights.label: Facility types
financialHighlights.note: A member lender approves the credit and sets the rate, capped at its base rate plus 3 percentage points.

overview: Helps eligible SC entrepreneurs access institutional credit by providing a guarantee to participating banks and financial institutions. IFCI Ltd operates the scheme.
keyBenefits: Guarantee support is provided to member lending institutions, not as money paid directly to the applicant
Covers eligible term loans, composite term loans, and working-capital facilities
Borrower interest is set by the member lender, linked to its base rate, and capped at 3 percentage points above that base rate
For eligible SC-owned businesses in manufacturing and services
mandatoryDocuments: SC certificate and business ownership records
Business registration and financial records
Project report and lender documents
The participating lender and IFCI may require further records
eligibilityBullets: The entrepreneur must belong to the Scheduled Caste community
SC entrepreneurs must hold more than 51% ownership with management control for at least 6 months
The enterprise must operate in manufacturing or services
Credit must be considered by a participating member lending institution
repaymentTerms: The borrower repays the loan to the lender under the lender’s approved terms; the guarantee does not set a borrower interest rate.

name: Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme
categoryTag: New microenterprise with bank credit and subsidy

financialHighlights.label: Project ceiling
financialHighlights.note: Project ceiling for eligible new units; specific activities have additional rules.

financialHighlights.label: Margin-money subsidy
financialHighlights.note: Rate depends on beneficiary category and whether the unit is urban or rural.

financialHighlights.label: Applicant contribution
financialHighlights.note: The bank finances the remaining eligible project cost; subsidy is subject to scheme conditions.

overview: Bank-financed support for setting up eligible new microenterprises in the non-farm sector. A government margin-money subsidy is adjusted through the bank loan account after scheme requirements are met.
keyBenefits: For new viable microenterprises; no family-income ceiling is listed
Maximum project cost is ₹50 lakh for manufacturing and ₹20 lakh for service projects
Subsidy ranges from 15% to 35%, based on category and rural or urban location
The bank assesses project viability and sets the loan terms
mandatoryDocuments: Aadhaar and identity/address proof
Project report and quotations
Education proof when the project exceeds the published threshold
Category or special-category proof when claiming a higher subsidy rate
Bank-specific KYC and application records
eligibilityBullets: Applicant must be over 18 years of age; one person per family may receive new-unit assistance
New units only for the primary assistance; already subsidized units are not eligible for this route
At least VIII standard education is required above ₹10 lakh manufacturing or ₹5 lakh service project cost
Projects must include capital expenditure and must not be on the scheme negative list; trading and transport activities have additional restrictions
availabilityNote: Check the PMEGP portal for current application windows, activity restrictions, and bank-specific terms.

name: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY / MUDRA)

financialHighlights.label: Kishore · Tarun
financialHighlights.note: Kishore runs to ₹5 lakh; Tarun runs above ₹5 lakh through ₹10 lakh.

financialHighlights.label: Tarun Plus
financialHighlights.note: Only for entrepreneurs who have successfully repaid a previous Tarun-category loan.

overview: Collateral-free institutional credit for income-generating microenterprises in manufacturing, trading, services, and eligible agriculture-allied activities. Banks and other member lenders set the final rate and terms.
keyBenefits: Supports both term-loan and working-capital needs
Loan categories run from Shishu through Tarun; Tarun Plus can reach ₹20 lakh after successful repayment of an earlier Tarun loan
No collateral is required under PMMY
Interest rates and repayment schedules are set by the lender
mandatoryDocuments: KYC documents and bank account details
Business plan or project details
Cost estimates and quotations where relevant
Lender-specific application and credit records
eligibilityBullets: For eligible non-farm income-generating microenterprises, including specified agriculture-allied activities
Loans are provided through banks, NBFCs, and microfinance institutions
Tarun Plus is restricted to borrowers who successfully repaid a prior Tarun-category loan
There is no single scheme-wide interest rate; the lender assesses and sets terms
repaymentTerms: Set by the lending institution based on its credit and risk assessment.

name: PM Vishwakarma

financialHighlights.label: Credit support
financialHighlights.value: Up to ₹3 lakh in two tranches
financialHighlights.note: First tranche up to ₹1 lakh (18 months); second up to ₹2 lakh (30 months) after scheme conditions.

financialHighlights.label: Beneficiary rate
financialHighlights.note: Government interest subvention supports the concessional rate.

financialHighlights.label: Other support
financialHighlights.note: Toolkit e-voucher up to ₹15,000; training stipend and transport allowance are also listed.

overview: End-to-end support for artisans and craftspeople who work with their hands and tools in one of 18 notified trades, including recognition, training, toolkit support, credit, and marketing assistance.
keyBenefits: Recognition through a PM Vishwakarma certificate and ID card
Basic training of 5–7 days and advanced training of 15 days or more, with stipend and transport allowance
Toolkit incentive up to ₹15,000 through e-voucher
Collateral-free credit in two conditional tranches at a 5% beneficiary rate
mandatoryDocuments: Aadhaar and mobile-linked identity for registration
Trade and occupation details for local verification
Bank account details
Additional records requested during registration and verification
eligibilityBullets: Applicant must be an Indian citizen aged at least 18
Applicant must be actively engaged in one of the 18 listed traditional trades on the registration date
Only one member per family may apply; government employees and their family members are not eligible
Past government-scheme credit, loan defaults, and other household restrictions can affect eligibility; the second loan tranche depends on repayment and other milestones
repaymentTerms: First tranche: up to 18 months; second tranche: up to 30 months. Tranches have separate eligibility conditions.
availabilityNote: Registration and benefit access follow local verification and the current portal guidelines.

name: PM SVANidhi
corporation: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

financialHighlights.label: Progressive loan tranches
financialHighlights.note: Higher tranches depend on repayment of earlier loans.

financialHighlights.label: Repayment periods
financialHighlights.note: Monthly instalments; repayment period varies by tranche.

financialHighlights.label: Digital benefit
financialHighlights.note: Eligible vendors who repay on time may receive a 7% interest subsidy and digital-payment incentives.

overview: Collateral-free working-capital loans for eligible street vendors, with progressive loan tranches, interest subsidy, digital-payment incentives, and a UPI-linked RuPay credit card for qualifying vendors.
keyBenefits: First, second, and third loan tranches up to ₹15,000, ₹25,000, and ₹50,000
Lending period extended through 31 March 2030
7% interest subsidy on timely repayment under scheme rules
Eligible vendors who repay the second tranche may qualify for a UPI-linked RuPay credit card up to ₹30,000
mandatoryDocuments: Street-vendor identity or certificate of vending, where available
Aadhaar and KYC records
Bank account details and mobile number
Local-body or portal verification may be required
eligibilityBullets: Applicant must be a street vendor covered by the current scheme guidelines
Loan access and later tranches depend on local verification and repayment history
The lender assesses the application under its credit process
The restructured scheme extends coverage to additional town types in a graded manner
repaymentTerms: Monthly instalments; 12, 18, or 36 months depending on the loan tranche.
availabilityNote: The restructured lending period runs through 31 March 2030; coverage expansion is being phased in.

name: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme

financialHighlights.label: Capital subsidy
financialHighlights.note: Calculated on eligible institutional credit or eligible equipment cost, whichever is lower.

financialHighlights.label: Subsidy ceiling
financialHighlights.note: For eligible institutional finance up to ₹1 crore; subject to scheme rules.

financialHighlights.label: Eligible investment
financialHighlights.note: Manufacturing and service MSEs; trading activity is not eligible.

Applies to eligible institutional finance up to ₹1 crore for new plant and machinery or equipment
Available to qualifying SC/ST-owned MSEs in manufacturing and service sectors
Subsidy claims are submitted through the prime lending institution; trading-only activity is excluded

Sanctioned institutional term-loan documents
Plant or equipment invoices/quotations
Lender and nodal-agency forms and due-diligence records

Assistance is for new plant/machinery/equipment in manufacturing or service activity

name: National SC-ST Hub

financialHighlights.label: Credit linkage

overview: Professional and capacity-building support for SC/ST entrepreneurs and MSEs to strengthen public-procurement participation, market access, credit linkages, and enterprise readiness.
keyBenefits: Mentoring, handholding, and vendor-development programmes
Capacity-building and entrepreneurship support
Market and public-procurement linkages, including support toward the 4% SC/ST procurement sub-target
Credit facilitation and information about related sub-schemes
mandatoryDocuments: SC/ST identity and enterprise-ownership records, when required
Udyam/MSE registration for enterprise-specific services
Business profile and product/service details
Programme-specific application documents
